title: Chicago's Field Museum Hosts Diwali Celebration With Dance, Diyas and Ayurveda on November 15
excerpt: The museum's Cultural Programming series marks the festival of lights on Sunday, November 15, from 12:30 to 5 p.m., with classical dance, Bollywood performances, henna, diya decorating, and two science sessions — all included with admission.
body:
• The Field Museum celebrates Diwali on Sunday, November 15, 2026, from 12:30 to 5:00 p.m. CST, with Indian classical dance, Bollywood performances, henna, and a diya-decorating workshop.
  • All Diwali programming is included with regular museum admission, and the museum is open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. that day, with last entry at 4 p.m.
  • Two Grainger Science Hub sessions give the festival a science angle: one on Ayurveda and Dhanteras, and one on the science of light through diyas.
  • The museum is at 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605 — plan to arrive before the 12:30 p.m. start to catch the full programme.

Chicago's Field Museum is bringing back its Diwali celebration this Sunday, November 15, filling the museum with Indian classical dance, Bollywood performances, and hands-on activities for the festival of lights. The programme runs from 12:30 to 5:00 p.m. and is included with museum admission, according to the Field Museum's event page.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Sunday, November 15, 2026
  • Time: 12:30–5:00 p.m. CST
  • Venue: Field Museum
  • Address: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
  • Admission: Diwali programming is included with museum admission
  • Official page: Celebrate Diwali at the Field Museum

What's On

The afternoon's programming mixes performance with activities visitors can join: Indian classical dance and Bollywood performances, interactive cultural activities, henna, and a diya-decorating workshop, per the Chicago Asian Network's Diwali guide. The event is part of the museum's Cultural Programming series and is open to all ages.

Two sessions in the museum's Grainger Science Hub take the festival into the museum's home territory — science. "Rooted in Nature: Ayurveda, Plants & the Science of Well-Being" explores the history of Ayurveda, the traditional system of medicine rooted in South Asia, and its connection to Diwali: the festival's opening observance, Dhanteras, honours Dhanvantari, the Hindu deity associated with healing and Ayurveda. "The Science of Light: Discovering Diwali Through Diyas" looks at the festival's lamps themselves.

Making a Day of It

The Field Museum is open daily from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with last entry at 4:00 p.m., so families can take in the permanent halls before the Diwali programme begins at 12:30 p.m. The celebration was among the Chicago weekend picks in the Chicago Tribune's roundup of what to do in the city this week. Diwali itself fell on Sunday, November 8 this year; the museum's celebration the following Sunday gives families who marked the festival at home a second, public round of festivities.
